claim_judgments.rationale: C0000 accurately captures the general duration requirements for a flight review under 14 CFR 61.56(a), preserving the exceptions in paragraphs (b) and (f).
C0001 faithfully combines the mandatory curricular elements of the flight review specified in 14 CFR 61.56(a)(1) and (a)(2).
C0002 accurately captures the permission for glider pilots to substitute three instructional flights to traffic pattern altitude for the 1 hour of flight training under 14 CFR 61.56(b).

C0003 faithfully captures the prohibition against acting as pilot in command without a flight review and logbook endorsement within the preceding 24 calendar months under 14 CFR 61.56(c), retaining the exceptions.
C0004 accurately conveys the exemption from flight review requirements for pilots who have passed proficiency checks or practical tests conducted by specified entities under 14 CFR 61.56(d)(1).

C0005 accurately represents the exemptions from flight review based on practical tests passed for flight instructor certificates, ratings, recent experience, or reinstatement under 14 CFR 61.56(d)(2).
C0006 accurately states the exemption from flight review for persons completing phases of an FAA-sponsored pilot proficiency program within the specified period under 14 CFR 61.56(e).
C0007 captures the ground training exemption under 14 CFR 61.56(f) for flight instructor certificate holders meeting recent experience or completing an approved refresher course.
C0008 faithfully states the exemption from the flight review for student pilots undergoing training with a current solo flight endorsement under 14 CFR 61.56(g).
C0009 correctly captures the permission under 14 CFR 61.56(h) allowing flight review requirements to be accomplished in combination with § 61.57 and other recent experience requirements.
C0010 correctly represents the permission and condition under 14 CFR 61.56(i)(1) regarding the use of flight simulators and flight training devices in an approved part 142 course.
C0011 accurately reflects 14 CFR 61.56(i)(2) requiring takeoff and landing requirements of § 61.57 to be met unless the simulator is approved for landings.
C0012 accurately captures the requirement in 14 CFR 61.56(i)(3) that the simulator or training device represent an aircraft or set of aircraft for which the pilot is rated.
